Exercise real resolver graphs and current projections for punctuation variants in both slots plus generic punctuation/Unicode. Retain all prior pinned descriptor/group/replacement, exact completion-report declaration, launch, preview, refusal, disposition, history and edge-origin corrections.

priorFindings.summary: Dependency absorption previews saved ordering while Apply submits staged ordering.
priorFindings.invariant: Every preview and migration disclosure must describe the complete staged policy that Apply will submit.
evidence: apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1320 — the first preview includes moduleDraftOrdering.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1333 — after auto-enabling prerequisites, the second preview omits ordering.
apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:104 — omitted ordering falls back to committed policy.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1401 — Apply still submits moduleDraftOrdering.

Read-only source-function reproduction: staging Judge after Code Review and enabling a module with an auto-enabled prerequisite produced a displayed preview with ordering={} while the draft retained the owner edge. Staged removals of saved edges are likewise previewed incorrectly.

priorFindings.summary: Pending previews can restore changes after Discard.
priorFindings.invariant: Discard must invalidate outstanding draft requests so their responses cannot restore discarded state.
evidence: apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:3028 — Discard resets drafts and preview without advancing modulePreviewRequest.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1321 — the pending response therefore passes its request-generation check.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1331 — dependency absorption can replace the restored enabled IDs with discarded IDs.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1336 — an ordinary pending response can restore discarded ordering disclosure and re-enable Apply.

Read-only delayed-response reproduction: Discard restored committed enabled IDs; releasing a pending dependency preview re-staged the discarded child and parent modules. A pending ordering-only response also restored its discarded preview while ordering controls remained reset.

priorFindings.summary: Apply can confirm newer ordering edits against an older preview.
priorFindings.invariant: Apply and migration confirmation must be bound to the latest completed validation of the exact submitted draft.
evidence: apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1205 — ordering controls immediately mutate the draft and start asynchronous validation.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1315 — refresh leaves the previous valid preview and enabled Apply button in place while awaiting IPC.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1383 — confirmation displays the previous preview's migration impact.
apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1397 — submission reads the newer mutable draft.

Read-only delayed-response reproduction: while the displayed preview contained only Judge after Code Review, Apply remained enabled and submitted an additional Code Review after Pattern Review edge with confirmedMigration=true before its preview completed.

priorFindings.summary: Apply accepts undisclosed catalog or feature-model changes under an earlier migration confirmation.
priorFindings.invariant: The applied resolved policy and migration baseline must match the policy and impact explicitly previewed and confirmed; external changes must invalidate that confirmation.
evidence: apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1367 — captures only enabled IDs, ordering and the saved-policy digest; apps/desktop/renderer/renderer.js:1438 submits those values.
apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:284 — saved-policy digest does not bind unselected discovered definitions or the active feature lock.
apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:201 — candidate reloads discovered definitions; apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:109 selects every definition, including newly discovered disabled modules.

apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:290 — recomputes the candidate; apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:297 accepts the existing confirmation; apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:308 and apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:320 persist the recomputed policy and model.

Read-only in-memory manager reproduction using the real resolver and migration-impact builder, with persistence mocked: adding test/new-review after an ordering preview left the saved-policy digest unchanged. Displayed modulesAdded was [], but Apply selected the new disabled module and migrated with modulesAdded=[test/new-review].

Related in-memory reproduction: migrating the feature lock to Code Review after Pattern Review after preview also left the saved-policy digest unchanged. The confirmation disclosed only Judge changing; Apply additionally removed Code Review ordering and migrated from a different model hash.

priorFindings.summary: Journal progress during JOURNAL_LOCKED refusal can still leave failed Apply partially committed.
priorFindings.invariant: f4 — journal_locked leaves a failed apply partially committed. the manager saves workflow.json before migration and restores it only for model_migration_conflict. journal-lock refusal occurs before core mutation, so the saved policy changes while the feature lock/journal remain unchanged. reloading these saved choices disables unchanged apply and hides the outstanding migration preview.
evidence: apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:358 — policy published before migration.
plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/feature.js:327 — journal lock acquired before migration publication.
plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/journal.js:107 — existing lock throws JOURNAL_LOCKED.
apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:374 — JOURNAL_LOCKED rolls back only when subsequent model and journal reads match the baseline.
apps/desktop/main/module-policy.js:393 — unrelated journal advancement instead retains policy and reports reconciliation.

Read-only in-memory reproduction using the actual manager, real resolver and migration-impact builder with virtual persistence: the migration stub advanced only an unrelated journal event and threw JOURNAL_LOCKED; Apply rejected, new Judge ordering remained saved, and the feature model remained unchanged. The quiet-lock and reload portions of the earlier finding are fixed.

priorFindings.summary: Emitted schema-4 packets can block subsequent advisory preparation as unclassified history.
priorFindings.invariant: Packets emitted by the supported retry workflow must remain recognized workflow history during subsequent advisory preparation.
evidence: plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/boundary-retry.js:256 — emits schema-4 boundary manifests for disabled checks.

priorFindings.summary: Public Mermaid graphs collapse distinct valid IDs, turning owner dependencies into self-loops.
priorFindings.invariant: Every distinct supported graph node must retain a distinct rendered identity, and rendered relationships must preserve the resolved DAG's endpoints and topology.
evidence: plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/graph.js:4 and apps/desktop/resources/protocol/graph.js:4 — nodeId replaces all punctuation with underscores.
plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/graph.js:48 — newly rendered finalization nodes retain distinct module IDs before serialization.
plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/graph.js:174 and :178 — serialization collapses both node declarations and edge endpoints.

Read-only real-resolver reproduction: valid finalization modules example/check-one and example/check.one with owner ordering resolve separately, but modelGraph emits two declarations named finalization_module_example_check_one and an owner-ordering self-loop. currentGraph produces the equivalent collision.
Related read-only reproduction using validateModel and compiled boundary definitions: valid gates check-one and check.one collapse in both model and current-boundary Mermaid output.
